item.title: WordPress wp2shell RCE CVEs and SleeperGem RubyGems Supply Chain Attack
item.content:encoded:
Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-63030, CVE-2026-60137) WordPress Core Unauthenticated RCE via wp2shell — Must Read

WordPress released fixes for the wp2shell vulnerability chain, which enables unauthenticated remote code execution on default WordPress 6.9.0–6.9.4 and 7.0.0–7.0.1 sites, while 6.8.x sites still need patching for the SQL injection component. Administrators should verify updates to 6.8.6, 6.9.5, or 7.0.2 and review exposed sites for possible compromise.

  • wp2shell is an unauthenticated remote code execution chain in WordPress core that combines CVE-2026-63030, a REST API batch-route confusion issue, with CVE-2026-60137, a SQL injection in the author__not_in parameter of WP_Query.
  • The full remote code execution chain affects WordPress core versions 6.9.0 through 6.9.4 and 7.0.0 through 7.0.1, while WordPress 6.8.0 through 6.8.5 carries only the SQL injection component.
  • WordPress released fixed versions 6.8.6, 6.9.5, and 7.0.2 on July 17, 2026, and the 7.1 beta line is fixed in 7.1 beta2.
  • The article says defenders should verify that automatic updates completed, prioritize sites on 6.9.0 or later, restrict or block /wp-json/batch/v1 until patched, monitor logs, and review potentially affected sites for compromise.
  • CyCognito’s observed exposure was spread across sectors, led by Consumer Discretionary at 18.6%, Industrials at 15.8%, and Communication Services at 13.0%.

SleeperGem: RubyGems supply chain attack targets dormant maintainer accounts — Should Read

Attackers compromised dormant RubyGems maintainer accounts to publish malicious gem updates that downloaded and executed payloads on developer machines while avoiding CI environments. The incident shows RubyGems is now facing the same dormant-account supply chain abuse long seen in npm and PyPI.

  • A new RubyGems package named git_credential_manager published four versions in rapid succession and downloaded binaries from a Git repository hosted at https://git.disroot.org/git-ecosystem/.
  • Version 2.8.0 of git_credential_manager acted as a dropper by building a hardcoded URL, disabling SSL certificate verification, fetching a payload, and executing it with a shell or PowerShell.
  • Version 2.8.2 wired the installer into the gem’s load path so that merely requiring git_credential_manager could trigger the installation flow, and version 2.8.3 uncommented the line that executed the downloaded script.
  • The package included a skip_install? check for roughly 30 CI-related environment variables, including GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Travis, Jenkins, and Vercel, and did nothing when it found one.
  • The attacker added git_credential_manager as a dependency to newly published versions of Dendreo and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab, with the latter belonging to a different maintainer and having 574,661 total downloads.
